content.text:
I rewrote `0.html`. It looks the same as before (a 400px black circle in the middle of the page), but it now behaves better on different screens. I haven't opened it in a browser to check.

- **No stray scrollbars:** the page was set to exactly `100vw` × `100vh`, which can add a horizontal scrollbar on desktop and clip content on mobile when the browser's address bar shows or hides. It now uses a minimum height (`min-height: 100dvh`, with `100vh` as a fallback for older browsers).
- **Fits small screens:** the circle was always 400px, so it overflowed phones and short windows. It now shrinks to fit (`min(400px, 100vw, 100vh)`) and stays round.
- **Simpler centering:** a two-line grid replaces the three-line flexbox.
- **Box sizing:** I added `box-sizing: border-box` to the reset, so any padding or borders you add later won't change element sizes.
- **Screen readers:** the circle now has `role="img"` and a `<title>`, so screen readers announce it instead of skipping it or reading it oddly.
- **Easier to recolor:** the fill is now `currentColor`, so setting a CSS `color` on the SVG or its parent changes the circle's color. It's still black by default.

If the circle is purely decorative, replace `role`/`aria-labelledby`/`<title>` with `aria-hidden="true"`. If you had something else in mind by "improve", like animation, dark mode or changing the design, tell me and I'll do that.
